canonical_statement: If X is a subset of R^n definable in an o-minimal structure over the real field, then for every epsilon > 0 there is c > 0 such that N(X - X_alg, T) <= c*T^epsilon for every T >= 1.

source_pinpoint.work: J. Pila and A. J. Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke Math. J. 133 (2006), 591-616

domain_and_universes: L : FirstOrder.Language.{0,0}; L.Structure Real; n : Nat; X : Set (Fin n -> Real); epsilon c : Real; T : Nat; root in Prop
conclusion: The bounded-height rational slice outside algebraicPart X is finite and its ncard, coerced to Real, is at most c * T ^ epsilon.

killed: moved the constant outside the structure/set/exponent binders

degenerate_cases: T=0 is excluded by T>=1. n=0 remains admitted and has coordinate maximum height zero. Empty sets and zero-dimensional sets remain admitted. epsilon<=0 is excluded. The constant is required positive.
status_boundary: Exact statement-only evidence; anchor, proof, trust, human-source audit, readability, hermetic replay, and independent acceptance remain open.
